issues.body:
**Credit name.** Joost de Winter, Delft University of Technology.

**Claim.** A packing of 297 unit squares in a square of side 17.739455558289 (rounded up at 12 places). The exact rational side is in the certificate. The record holds 17.740417287543801851 for n = 297 (T-174) at commit 7629f5adede4c38f006e355281ea76340120fd94. The gain is 0.00096.

**Certificate.** Exact rational coordinates of all 297 squares (centre and unit edge direction) and the side, in the folder `n297` of https://github.com/JoostdeWinter/square-packing at commit 7b4701f35e815301e4f467d214fab4205ded5eb1.

- `n297/n297_exact.json`
- `n297/n297_witness.yaml` (the same packing as a Witness/v2 file, center-basis, rational)

A figure of T-174 and the new packing side by side is in `n297/n297_before_after.png`.

**Checking.**

1. `n297/verify_exact.py`. Arithmetic: Python `fractions.Fraction`. It checks that every edge direction is a unit vector, that every square lies in the container, and that every pair of squares with centres closer than sqrt(2) is separated along an edge direction of one of the two squares. It reports 297 squares and 632 close pairs. Command: `python3 -B verify_exact.py` in the folder `n297`. Cost: about 2 seconds on one core.
2. `n297/check_area.py`. Arithmetic: Python `fractions.Fraction`. It clips one square of each close pair against the other and requires an intersection of area exactly 0. It reports 297 squares and 632 close pairs. Command: `python3 -B check_area.py` in the folder `n297`. Cost: about 1 second on one core.
3. The witness file validates against `packing/witnesses/witness.schema.yaml` at the commit of this repository named above (jsonschema, 0 errors).

**What the checkers share.** One author, Python's `Fraction` type and the same input file. The two scripts share no code. The first uses a separating-axis test and the second uses the area of the clipped intersection.

**Not done.** The certificate has not been checked with this project's own tools. The statement that the packing is a local optimum of its arrangement rests on numerical work: two series of random restarts ended at the same side, a linear program over all 297 squares found no first-order improvement, and the rational side is 1.8e-59 above the 330-digit solution of the 4289 contact equations. A proof of local or global optimality is missing.

**Lineage and credit.** The layout is that of T-174 (found by Francisco Couzo, improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd): two blocks of axis-aligned squares with staircase edges, two corner blocks of 10 squares, and a diagonal band of 18 columns of tilted squares. Two things are new. First, each staircase has two steps of double size. Between them the band lies one staircase step closer to the upper left block, and a column of 7 squares sits at each double step. The upper left block has 6 squares fewer than in T-174, the lower right block has 4 more, and the band has 2 more. Second, the band columns change lean direction once, where T-174 changes three times. The double step was taken from the staircases of the pinwheel packings T-292 and T-293 (n = 132 and n = 157). Please credit the result to Joost de Winter as a packing that builds on T-174.

**AI assistance.** The construction, optimization, high-precision solution, rational certificate, checks and figures were produced with Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic) under my direction.

issues.body:
**Credit name.** Joost de Winter, Delft University of Technology.

**Claim.** A packing of 332 unit squares in a square of side 18.739455558289 and a packing of 409 unit squares in a square of side 20.739455558289 (both rounded up at 12 places). The exact rational sides are in the certificates. The record holds 18.740417287544 for n = 332 and 20.740417290708 for n = 409 at commit 7629f5adede4c38f006e355281ea76340120fd94. The gain is 0.00096 for each.

**Certificate.** Exact rational coordinates of all squares (centre and unit edge direction) and the side, in the folder `above324_from_n297` of https://github.com/JoostdeWinter/square-packing at commit c70defaf39af47db220d1e7c2922590637ffb664.

- `above324_from_n297/n332_exact.json`
- `above324_from_n297/n409_exact.json`

**Checking.**

1. `above324_from_n297/verify_exact.py`. Arithmetic: Python `fractions.Fraction`. It checks that every edge direction is a unit vector, that every square lies in the container, and that every pair of squares with centres closer than sqrt(2) is separated along an edge direction of one of the two squares. It reports 332 squares with 729 close pairs and 409 squares with 875 close pairs. Command: `python3 -B verify_exact.py n332_exact.json` (or `n409_exact.json`) in the folder. Cost: a few seconds on one core.
2. `above324_from_n297/check_area.py`. Arithmetic: Python `fractions.Fraction`. It clips one square of each close pair against the other and requires an intersection of area exactly 0. It reports the same counts. Command: `python3 -B check_area.py n332_exact.json` (or `n409_exact.json`). Cost: a few seconds on one core.

**What the checkers share.** One author, Python's `Fraction` type and the same input files. The two scripts share no code.

**Not done.** The certificates have not been checked with this project's own tools.

**Lineage and credit.** Both packings are the packing of 297 squares from my registration request for n = 297 (folder `n297` of the same repository), which builds on T-174 (found by Francisco Couzo, improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd). For n = 332, 35 axis-aligned squares are added along two walls. For n = 409, two arms of 3 x 17 axis-aligned squares and 10 squares in the corner are added. Five of these 10 lie in a square of side 2.72, one of them tilted by 45 degrees. This follows the construction of the recorded values for 332 and 409. Please credit the results to Joost de Winter as packings that build on T-174.

**AI assistance.** The construction and the checks were produced with Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic) under my direction.
